prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, which made the synthesis of aryl amines general and routine

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B021 alone, Buchwald and Hartwig. The chair asked for the new principle in C-N coupling so that it can be tested. Reductive elimination of a C-N bond from palladium is intrinsically slow, and amido complexes with beta-hydrogens decompose by beta-hydride elimination to arene and imine. The 2010 prize rewarded a framework in which C-C bonds form from organometallic nucleophiles by transmetalation. C-N coupling is not that reaction with a different partner. It needed a different elementary-step problem to be solved, which was the rate of C-N reductive elimination relative to beta-hydride elimination, and the answer was ligand design: bulky chelating and then bulky monodentate biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines, with an amine-deprotonation step that has no counterpart in Suzuki or Negishi chemistry. That mechanism was worked out independently by both laureates and is confirmed by three decades of independent use, several ligand and precatalyst generations, and routine pharmaceutical process application. It remains the cleanest combination of novelty of mechanism, maturity and attribution on this shortlist. Round 1 did not show a majority for anything, so I weigh the scientific case and not the counts. On that basis, nothing I read persuades me to trade a settled, documented advance for a candidate with an open attribution or maturity question.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection stands: a committee that regards the 2010 prize as having honoured the principle of palladium cross-coupling will read C-N coupling as an extension, and Chabes and Aqvist have said so. Kosugi's earlier Pd/tin amide chemistry is a precursor whose exact role a citation should handle with care. The prize would also be a pure synthetic-methodology award, which some members may prefer to balance with a more biological or physical topic, and it has the narrowest support in the openings among the leading candidates.

responses.point: Chabes sees B021 as an extension of an already honoured field, and prefers sequencing by synthesis (B028) with Balasubramanian and Klenerman after dropping Rothberg.
responses.response: I take the extension argument seriously, and I answer it with mechanism. The 2010 citation covers C-C coupling by transmetalation. C-N coupling needed a different solution, ligands that accelerate C-N reductive elimination and suppress beta-hydride elimination, and that is why it took until 1994-95 and a decade of ligand work after the C-C reactions were known. On B028 I agree that the chemistry is real, since reversible terminators and surface chemistry are genuinely chemical, and I accept your decision to drop Rothberg. My remaining concern is that a two-name cut leaves Ju and Mayer with parallel claims, so I cannot call the attribution as settled as Buchwald and Hartwig, but I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Aqvist treats C-N coupling as a successful application of an existing principle, ranks it outside his top eight, and proposes Liu alone for base editing paired with Car and Parrinello.
responses.response: Applying an existing principle would describe a new substrate scope under the same ligands. Here the ligands, the base-mediated amine activation and the choice of elementary step were new, which is why the field was not simply following Heck and Suzuki. On B052 I agree that Liu's role is unambiguous and I keep it as my first alternative. My objection is attribution and maturity. Liu alone leaves Kondo and Nishida's near-contemporaneous deaminase work unaddressed, and the clinical record is a decade old. On B019 I accept the quality of the theory and four decades of validation, but the lasting method is now Born-Oppenheimer dynamics, and pairing it with an unrelated biology topic weakens the coherence of the prize in my view.

responses.point: Somfai supports Buchwald and Hartwig, treats Kosugi as background to the citation text and not a laureate, and notes that our views converge on B021 and little else.
responses.response: We agree on the two names and on Kosugi. I would draft the citation around the catalytic, ligand-controlled method and not mention the stoichiometric precursor in the laureate line. Your note that the support is narrow is fair, and the committee cannot ignore that. It is a reason to resolve the 2010 question explicitly in discussion, not a reason to treat B021 as weaker on science. If members who ranked it low are persuaded that the elementary-step problem is distinct, the support should widen. If not, the vote should show that.

responses.point: Sparr pairs condensates (B044) with Cullis for lipid nanoparticles (B058), arguing the two-part prize is balanced across physical and biological chemistry and that B058 has the broadest support.
responses.response: The breadth of support for B058 is real, and I respect that the lipid design principle (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids) is chemical. But I cannot support Cullis alone as an exact credit while Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer all have documented contributions. A prize that is clean on paper and arguably unfair to the people who made the lipids is not better than the one I propose. For B044 I share the concern about equilibrium phase separation in living cells and the omission of Rosen, Pappu and Mittag. I think the answer to the chair's coherence question is that one well-defined achievement beats two bridged ones, so I stay with a single part.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler first on long-range electron transfer, and lists B021 as an alternative.
responses.response: The chair asked whether B017 would be considered by members who did not rank it. I did not rank it in the opening, and I find the pair clean and the physics mechanism-level and well confirmed. The experimental case, measured rates against distance and driving force with Ru-modified proteins, is the kind of structural evidence I look for. But Marcus already received his prize, and the theoretical framework that makes the experiments readable is spread beyond the credited pair. I would put it ahead of some candidates on this list but not ahead of B021, where both the method and its reach across chemistry are demonstrated.

uncertainties: Whether a majority regards the C-N reductive-elimination and beta-hydride-elimination problem as a distinct principle from 2010 C-C coupling, which I argue from my reading of the mechanistic literature and cannot settle by evidence in this room.
How the citation should treat Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide precursor and the earlier Migita work, which I treat as background from recollection and not as independently checked priority history.

Whether the committee will prefer a materials, structural or biology-facing prize this year over a synthetic-methodology one, in which case my first alternatives (B052, B003) matter more than they do now.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal applies to B021, B052 or B003. I have no known connection to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi, Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo, Nishida, or the perovskite groups. My ties to porous-materials and electron-crystallography communities and my Stockholm University colleague relationship with Secretary Brzezinski do not bear on any named laureate, and I disclose them unchanged from round 1.
